Q: Extra row with blank values created with MS Graph when inserting into Sharepoint list A:

From what you've shared, I don't see anything in the code that would cause PostAsync() to create two items. That call should only send a single POST request to Microsoft Graph.

Since you've already confirmed the method is only being hit once, I'd start looking outside the C# code. A few things worth checking:

  • Whether there's a Power Automate flow or SharePoint workflow that's triggered when an item is created.

  • Any event receivers, webhooks, or customizations on the site that might be creating another item.

  • Enable Graph SDK logging (or use a tool like Fiddler) to verify that only one HTTP POST is actually leaving your application.

If only one request is being sent but two items appear in the list, then the extra blank item is likely being created on the SharePoint side rather than by your code.

Nothing in the request body you've posted looks like it would explain the duplicate insert, especially if similar code works correctly with other lists.

Q: Distinct by property A:

If you only need the distinct property values, and not the objects, you can do the following:

person.stream().map(person -> p.getName()).distinct()

It will only work if your property values override equals, which most base types do.

Q: When does type binding happen in Rust? A:

Types in rust, like in C/C++ are determined at compile time.

However, the process of determining types in rust is substantially more complex than in C. In C the process of determining types flows through an expression in the same direction as the data. In rust type inteference can and often does flow in both directions. Sometimes different parts of a type may be determined from different places.

for example

let v = Vec::new(); // establishes that v is a Vec, but not what the element type is.
v.push(1u32); // establishes that the element type is u32

Your compiler will need to be able to represent the idea of a variable whose type is not yet known, or is only partially known.

Q: how to authenticate domain credential in powershell script A:

As suggested by @vonPryz running the script in an authenticated remote session is probably the best thing to. Regarding your concern that Get-Credential is needed for instantiating a remote session and asks for username and password, there are at least two options:

  1. Creating PSCredential on the fly
  2. Reading encrypted credentials from disk

Creating PSCredential on the fly

Creating credentials from clear text passwords is described here: Creating a PS Credential from a Clear Text Password in Powershell

You basically run:

PS C:\> $password = "P@ssw0rd" | ConvertTo-SecureString -asPlainText -Force
PS C:\> $username = "EdgarSchnittenfittich" 
PS C:\> $credential = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential($username,$password)

Reading encrypted credentials from disk

Once you have a PSCredential object you can export it in an encrypted form via Export-CliXml. To import your credentials just issue Import-CliXml. The credentials are store in an encrypted form with an opaque encryption key for the current user exporting the credentials. This means that only the same user can later on import the credentials again.

Example:

$cred = Get-PSCredential;
$cred | Export-CliXml C:\TEMP\Credentials.xml;

$importedCredentials = Import-CliXml C:\TEMP\Credentials.xml;

Running your Scripts

  • With these credentials you can easily run any script via Enter-PSSession or Invoke-Command.
  • Regarding your Jenkins environment: make sure you export the encrypted credentials under the same service account that you use to import your credentials.

Q: DataTable Error: Uncaught ReferenceError: jQuery is not defined A:

According to Datatables.net

DataTables has only one library dependency (other software upon which it relies in order to work) - jQuery. Being a jQuery plug-in, DataTables makes use of many of the excellent features that jQuery provides, and hooks into the jQuery plug-in system, in the same way as all other jQuery plug-ins. jQuery 1.7 or newer will work with DataTables, although typically you will want to use the latest version. DataTables includes everything else that it requires to operate.

Update your jQuery to the newest version and try again. Also remove the 

jQuery(function ($) {
});

in the main JS. You don't need it.

Q: Watch app won't install on watchOS 26.5 — "The app could not be installed at this time" A:

This is a known Apple regression in watchOS 26.5/26.5.1 — see Apple Developer Forums thread 827053 (FB22807635), where Apple confirmed it as "a regression we have known." No shipped release fixes it as of July 2026.

The broken piece is the phone→watch transfer link (Identity Services over Bluetooth). The workaround is to bypass it and push the app over WiFi from a Mac:

1. Turn the iPhone's Bluetooth off and leave it off. This forces the watch onto WiFi so the Mac↔Watch CoreDevice tunnel can come up — a quick toggle is not enough. Keep Mac, iPhone, and watch on the same WiFi network (not a Personal Hotspot).

2. Install with devicectl:

xcrun devicectl device install app --device <WATCH-COREDEVICE-ID> --timeout 240 \
  "~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/<App>/Build/Products/Release-watchos/<Watch App>.app"

Get the watch ID from xcrun devicectl list devices. Use the Release-watchos build product (no __preview.dylib). Keep --timeout 240 — the first tunnel bring-up is slow.

Two gotchas:

  • devicectl device info details can report stale tunnelState=None even after a successful install. Trust the install command's App installed output.

  • The Xcode "Run" stall is unrelated: the shared-cache symbol download it blocks on is debugger support only, which is why devicectl succeeds while Xcode hangs.

The Bluetooth toggle on both devices has resolved this for some users (see the linked thread), so it's worth 30 seconds before my full workaround.
